GRU4Rec’s original [top-k loss paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) directly addresses easy-negative saturation: ordinary BPR dilutes gradients across negatives, whereas BPR-max emphasizes high-scoring negatives through softmax weights and adds negative-score regularization. BPR-max already performs implicit hard-negative weighting; explicit mining must demonstrate additional benefit. [Sampled-softmax research (2024)](https://zlstwebsite.github.io/Zlst/publication/on-the-effectiveness-of-sampled-softmax-loss-for-item-recommendation/) identifies informative hard-negative gradients and ranking benefits, but also warns that cosine scoring can impair representation-magnitude learning. These findings motivate a GRU experiment; they do not establish superiority on this benchmark.

Hardness and sampling bias interact. [UFNRec (SDM 2023)](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/1.9781611977653.ch6) shows that sampled negatives can contain useful latent positives, motivating caution about aggressively penalizing the highest-scoring unlabeled items. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent sampling tradeoffs: random sampling favors head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an aggregate-performance cost. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) further shows that standard in-batch correction overlooks the positive item’s guaranteed inclusion; sampling correction must match the actual proposal mechanism.

Practical hypothesis: compare uniform-pool BPR-max against sampled cross-entropy using identical candidate pools, negative counts and compute limits; then separately test tempered hard-negative weighting with uniform exploration. Exclude observed training positives, and treat downweighting suspicious negatives as an ablation rather than reliable false-negative identification. Keep one GRU/checkpoint per category. Select exclusively through fixed four-category macro validation HR@10: improved training separation alone does not establish better ranking against competitive candidates.
